nodes.label: Bottom-up Attentional Capture
nodes.definition: Priority allocation toward salient or otherwise attention-attracting events that can occur even when those events are not aligned with the current task goal.
exclusions: learned selection-history effects when those are the primary mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Competition for attentional priority can favor salient events; control depends on interaction with goals and selection history.
failure_modes: Treating salience as sufficient for guaranteed attention
Assuming capture is fully independent of goals/context
open_questions: Operational boundary with novelty orienting and selection-history capture

nodes.label: Working-Memory Capacity
nodes.definition: Limited capacity for maintaining and using currently relevant information under task demands.
inclusions: capacity constraints relevant to active processing
nodes.mechanism_summary: Working-memory limitations constrain active representation and interact with attentional control.
failure_modes: Equating one task score with universal capacity
Treating capacity as identical to cognitive load
open_questions: Task-general versus task-specific capacity modeling

nodes.label: Expectancy of Success
nodes.definition: A person's expectation or belief about the likelihood of succeeding at a task or attaining a goal.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Expectancy contributes to motivational choice, effort or persistence in combination with value and context.
failure_modes: Treating expectancy as value
Assuming high expectancy always increases action regardless of value/cost
open_questions: Boundary with self-efficacy and perceived control

nodes.label: Goal-Relevance Appraisal
nodes.definition: Evaluation of whether an event or situation bears on the person's goals, concerns, or well-being.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal of personal significance contributes to emotional differentiation and action tendencies.
failure_modes: Using emotional label as proof of the underlying appraisal
Confusing goal relevance with positive valence
open_questions: Interaction with novelty, controllability and certainty appraisals

nodes.label: Group Identification
nodes.definition: The degree to which a group membership is psychologically incorporated into the self and becomes relevant to perception and behavior.
inclusions: strength of identification with a group
nodes.mechanism_summary: Identification can change the relevance of group norms and referent influence.
failure_modes: Inferring strong identification from membership alone
Treating all group effects as identity effects
open_questions: State versus chronic identification in commercial contexts

nodes.label: Injunctive Norm
nodes.definition: A perceived or communicated socially shared view about what people should or should not do.
exclusions: formal legal rule unless socially represented as a norm
nodes.mechanism_summary: Injunctive norms can guide behavior through internalization or anticipated social enforcement, with important reactance/autonomy boundaries.
failure_modes: Confusing what others do with what others approve
Assuming norm messaging cannot backfire
open_questions: Conditions producing reactance or undermining intrinsic motivation

nodes.label: Risk Perception
nodes.definition: Subjective judgment about the possibility and/or severity of uncertain adverse outcomes.
exclusions: probability weighting as a specific mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Risk perception contributes to judgment under uncertainty but is analytically distinct from preference and final choice.
failure_modes: Equating perceived risk with objective probability
Inferring risk aversion from high risk perception
open_questions: Decomposition into likelihood versus severity across domains

nodes.label: Attribute Trade-Off Conflict
nodes.definition: Conflict arising when alternatives differ on attributes or goals such that improvement on one dimension requires sacrifice on another.
exclusions: simple preference with no competing attributes
opportunity cost awareness as a separate process
nodes.mechanism_summary: Trade-off structure shapes whether decision makers balance attributes, choose compromise options, or adopt more extreme solutions.
failure_modes: Treating all multiattribute choice as experienced conflict
Assuming a single universal compromise response
open_questions: Moderators of mixed versus extreme resolution

nodes.label: Attitudinal Ambivalence
nodes.definition: Coexistence of positive and negative evaluative tendencies toward the same attitude object.
exclusions: uncertainty caused only by lack of knowledge
neutral attitude with no positive or negative evaluation
nodes.mechanism_summary: Ambivalence is an attitude-structure property that can affect certainty, processing and resistance.
failure_modes: Equating ambivalence with neutrality
Equating ambivalence with low confidence
open_questions: Objective versus subjective ambivalence and their runtime relevance

nodes.label: Attitude–Behavior Consistency
nodes.definition: The degree to which an attitude corresponds with or predicts relevant behavior under specified conditions.
exclusions: mere attitude strength without behavioral observation
nodes.mechanism_summary: Attitudes do not map mechanically to behavior; context, self-interest, control and other moderators can affect consistency.
failure_modes: Using attitude change as proof of behavioral change
Substituting intention for observed behavior
open_questions: Which moderators are most useful for copywriting runtime inference

nodes.label: Common Ground
nodes.definition: Information that communicators treat as shared background for the purposes of their interaction.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Language interpretation and audience design can depend on what information is treated as shared, using mechanisms whose efficiency varies with context and cognitive demands.
failure_modes: Assuming the audience actually shares what the writer presupposes
Equating common ground with demographic similarity
open_questions: How to infer common ground safely from customer research

nodes.label: Situation-Model Construction
nodes.definition: Construction of a mental representation of the situation described by discourse, beyond the surface wording and local propositions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Comprehenders integrate discourse and knowledge into a representation that supports coherence and inference.
failure_modes: Assuming comprehension from surface recall alone
Treating situation models as directly observable without task-specific inference
open_questions: Best operational proxies for commercial message comprehension

nodes.label: Narrative Transportation
nodes.definition: A state in which a recipient becomes mentally immersed in the world evoked by a narrative.
inclusions: narrative immersion as operationalized in transportation research
nodes.mechanism_summary: Transportation is a narrative-processing construct with empirically studied antecedents, moderators and persuasive consequences.
failure_modes: Equating engagement metrics with transportation
Assuming every story transports every audience
open_questions: Channel and audience moderators relevant to copy runtime

nodes.label: Refutational Two-Sided Message
nodes.definition: A persuasive message that acknowledges opposing considerations and explicitly refutes or answers them.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Message-sidedness effects depend on whether opposing arguments are refuted and on message/context characteristics.
failure_modes: Assuming two-sidedness is universally more persuasive
Treating concession without refutation as equivalent
open_questions: Boundary conditions by product category, audience position and time pressure

nodes.label: Processing Fluency
nodes.definition: The subjective ease with which information is processed.
exclusions: mere familiarity as a cause rather than the fluency experience
nodes.mechanism_summary: Fluency can inform judgment through affective or interpretive pathways; meaning depends on context and attribution.
failure_modes: Assuming fluent means true or good
Equating readability with fluency
Equating fluency with comprehension
open_questions: Perceptual versus conceptual subtypes and copy-specific moderators

nodes.label: Autonomous Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivation experienced with a sense of willingness, volition and personal endorsement, including intrinsic motivation and sufficiently internalized extrinsic motivation.
inclusions: identified/integrated forms of extrinsic regulation when genuinely endorsed
nodes.mechanism_summary: The quality/source of regulation differs from motivation amount and can affect persistence and experience.
failure_modes: Treating autonomy as absence of external context
Equating autonomous with intrinsic only
open_questions: Transport from work/education to consumer action contexts

nodes.label: Controlled Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivation regulated by external or internal pressure, contingencies, demands or controlling reasons rather than full personal endorsement.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Controlled regulation can produce action while differing functionally from autonomous motivation.
failure_modes: Equating controlled motivation with extrinsic motivation universally
Assuming controlled motivation cannot produce behavior
open_questions: Conditions under which persuasive pressure shifts autonomous to controlled regulation

nodes.label: Descriptive Norm
nodes.definition: A perception or communication about what relevant others typically do.
exclusions: simple popularity without a relevant social referent
nodes.mechanism_summary: Descriptive norms provide social information about common behavior and can differ from injunctive expectations.
failure_modes: Confusing prevalence with approval
Treating platform popularity as a validated norm measure
open_questions: Referent proximity and domain moderators

nodes.label: Reference Point
nodes.definition: A comparison standard relative to which outcomes or changes in value are evaluated.
exclusions: anchor used only for numeric estimation
objective baseline with no psychological comparison role
nodes.mechanism_summary: Reference-dependent evaluation can change sensitivity to gains/losses or changes relative to a comparison standard.
failure_modes: Assuming the status quo is always the operative reference
Assuming a single reference point
open_questions: How multiple reference points are selected in commercial choice

nodes.label: Loss Aversion
nodes.definition: Greater sensitivity to losses than comparable gains relative to an operative reference point.
inclusions: loss-gain asymmetry conditional on reference point
nodes.mechanism_summary: Loss aversion is one possible reference-dependent asymmetry; robustness and generality vary by paradigm and reference-point structure.
failure_modes: Treating loss aversion as a universal law
Explaining every negative framing effect as loss aversion
open_questions: Domain robustness and reference-point moderators

nodes.label: Perceived Source Expertise
nodes.definition: Perceived competence or ability of a source to provide valid information within the relevant domain.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Expertise is a source-credibility dimension whose persuasive impact depends on receiver/message/context conditions.
failure_modes: Treating credentials as guaranteed perceived expertise
Assuming expertise always increases persuasion
open_questions: Interaction with prior attitudes and elaboration

nodes.label: Perceived Source Trustworthiness
nodes.definition: Perceived honesty, integrity or lack of deceptive intent attributed to a source in the relevant communication context.
exclusions: relational trust as a broad interpersonal history unless source evaluation is the target
nodes.mechanism_summary: Trustworthiness is a distinct source-credibility dimension and its effect is context-dependent.
failure_modes: Equating trustworthiness with expertise
Assuming familiar/liked sources are necessarily trustworthy
open_questions: Interaction with transparency and persuasion knowledge

nodes.label: Metaphor Comprehension
nodes.definition: Processes by which a listener or reader derives intended figurative meaning from metaphorical expressions.
exclusions: analogy used purely as argumentative structure
nodes.mechanism_summary: Multiple theoretical accounts—analogy, categorization and conceptual mapping—capture aspects of metaphor comprehension; no single mechanism is assumed universally.
failure_modes: Treating every metaphor as conceptual mapping only
Assuming figurative language improves comprehension by default
open_questions: Familiarity, novelty and complexity moderators

nodes.label: Two-Sided Message
nodes.definition: A persuasive message structure that presents both supporting and opposing or negative considerations about the advocated position/object.
exclusions: simple disclaimer unrelated to the advocated claim
nodes.mechanism_summary: Two-sidedness is a structural property; persuasive effects depend on refutation, amount/placement of negative information and receiver/context characteristics.
failure_modes: Assuming two-sided messages are universally superior
Equating any caveat with substantive two-sidedness
open_questions: Optimal use across sophistication/knowledge states and channels

nodes.label: Perceptual Salience
nodes.definition: Relative perceptual prominence of a stimulus feature or object that can bias selection priority.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceptual prominence contributes to competition for selection but does not guarantee capture.
failure_modes: Equating salience with actual attention
Inferring salience from engagement outcomes
open_questions: Cross-modal and naturalistic-copy salience

nodes.label: Attentional Set / Target Template
nodes.definition: An active representation of goal-relevant target properties that biases selective attention.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Goal-relevant representations alter competition for attentional selection.
failure_modes: Assuming a marketing persona proves an attentional set
open_questions: Naturalistic inference from search intent and task context

nodes.label: Executive Attentional Control
nodes.definition: Control processes that regulate attentional competition in accordance with task goals.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Executive control can bias selection and resolve interference while interacting with working-memory representations.
failure_modes: Treating one reaction-time score as global executive control
open_questions: Task-specific transport

nodes.label: Reward-Associated Attentional Priority
nodes.definition: Attentional priority acquired through prior associations between features and reward or learned value.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Learning history can persistently bias later selection, but magnitude is method-sensitive.
failure_modes: Using prior likes as direct evidence of value-driven capture
Assigning a universal effect coefficient
open_questions: Transport from visual-search paradigms to copy exposure

nodes.label: Prior-Selection History
nodes.definition: Bias in current attentional priority attributable to prior selections independently of current goals or physical salience.
exclusions: reward learning when reward association is the primary mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Past selection episodes can alter future priority.
failure_modes: Failing to control current goals/salience
open_questions: Duration and context specificity

nodes.label: Sustained Attention
nodes.definition: Maintenance of task-relevant attentional engagement over an extended interval.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Sustained attention concerns ongoing task-relevant processing rather than initial selection.
failure_modes: Inferring sustained attention from early hold or completion rate alone
open_questions: Naturalistic content-specific measurement

nodes.label: Vigilance Decrement
nodes.definition: Decline in performance or attentional maintenance as time-on-task increases under vigilance demands.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Performance may degrade over sustained monitoring time.
failure_modes: Calling any drop-off a vigilance decrement without task controls
open_questions: Applicability to media consumption

nodes.label: Attentional Disengagement
nodes.definition: Process of releasing or shifting attentional priority away from the currently selected target.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Disengagement governs release from current priority and can shape switching/reorientation.
failure_modes: Equating disengagement with suppression
open_questions: Naturalistic message transition effects

nodes.label: Certainty Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of how certain or predictable an event, cause, or outcome appears within an emotional episode.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Certainty appraisal contributes to differentiated emotional response patterns.
failure_modes: Confusing emotional certainty appraisal with epistemic confidence
open_questions: Commercial threat/opportunity contexts

nodes.label: Controllability / Coping-Potential Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of whether and how a person can control, cope with, or respond effectively to an event or its consequences.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceived control and coping potential contribute to emotion differentiation and action tendency.
failure_modes: Assuming objective control equals perceived control
open_questions: Interaction with fear/anger/hope in copy

nodes.label: Affective Arousal
nodes.definition: Degree of affective activation or energetic intensity, analytically separable from positive-negative valence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Arousal can alter readiness and, in some contexts, social transmission, but its meaning depends on appraisal and context.
failure_modes: Inferring emotion identity from arousal
Assuming high arousal guarantees sharing/action
open_questions: Channel and audience moderators

nodes.label: Approach Action Tendency
nodes.definition: Readiness or tendency to move toward, engage with, acquire, confront, or otherwise act in an approach-oriented direction.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal and affect can organize approach-oriented action readiness, but valence does not map one-to-one onto approach.
failure_modes: Equating positive affect with approach
open_questions: Distinct approach forms in commercial decisions

nodes.label: Withdrawal / Avoidance Action Tendency
nodes.definition: Readiness or tendency to withdraw from, avoid, escape, or disengage from a target or situation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal and affect can organize withdrawal/avoidance readiness, but negative valence does not map one-to-one onto avoidance.
failure_modes: Equating negative affect with avoidance
open_questions: Threat versus disgust versus effort-based avoidance

nodes.label: Self-Relevance
nodes.definition: Degree to which information, outcomes, or identities connect to a personally important aspect of the self.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-relevance can alter valuation, attention and processing by linking information to self-representations.
failure_modes: Inferring self-relevance from demographic targeting alone
open_questions: State versus chronic self-relevance

nodes.label: Self-Categorization
nodes.definition: Psychological classification of self as a member of a salient social category, affecting self-perception and social influence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Salient self-categorization can make group norms and prototypes self-relevant.
failure_modes: Inferring self-categorization from membership only
open_questions: Contextual activation in market segments

nodes.label: In-Group Prototypicality
nodes.definition: Degree to which a person, source, or position is perceived as representative of a salient in-group.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Prototypicality can shape who is influential when a group identity is salient.
failure_modes: Using surface similarity as proof of prototypicality
open_questions: Source prototypicality versus product prototypicality

nodes.label: Perceived Source Genuineness / Authenticity
nodes.definition: Perception that a source's self-presentation or communication is genuine rather than fabricated or strategically false in a way relevant to evaluation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Genuineness can contribute to source evaluation, especially in relational or influencer contexts, with contextual heterogeneity.
failure_modes: Treating casual tone as authenticity
Equating authenticity with factual accuracy
open_questions: Transport beyond creator/influencer contexts

nodes.label: Source Reliability Track Record
nodes.definition: Historical evidence or perception that a source has produced dependable outcomes or accurate/reliable information over time.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Past reliability can inform source evaluation but is domain-specific and evidence for an independent stable construct is not yet sufficient here.
failure_modes: Treating past reliability as guaranteed current accuracy
open_questions: Best construct placement versus evidence-traceability module
